A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ChatSOP and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Corresponding content can be reliably matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original dataset-quality measurements, SOP-prediction and dialogue-generation experiments in Tables 4–5, human evaluations, and appendix cost analysis.

after.justification: v4 retains those original evaluations and adds SOP-quality sensitivity results, a dual-planner baseline comparison, and runtime and monetary-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The DAL/TCoT/SFT offline planners, SOP-guided MCTS stages, prompts, and Algorithm 1 retain the same procedures. Describing SOP-pool edges as predicted clarifies existing construction. The revised experimental reward weight is a setting change, not a new algorithm component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Chinese SOPDAIL coverage: 53 tasks across 32 domains, covering SOP prediction and dialogue generation. The appendix task list is unchanged. New analyses vary planner configurations and SOP outputs within this coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 6 adds an unsupervised adaptation of He et al.'s dual-planner method, labeled DPDP in the table and PDPD in the prose, on GPT-4o and Qwen1.5-72b. The revised cost comparison drops CoT+SFT from v3 Figure 12. Existing main-table comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 changes the reported experimental reward weight lambda from 1 to 0.5, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. New evaluations vary SOP quality and specify an unsupervised, hyperparameter-aligned DPDP comparison; cost evaluation adds time and monetary metrics. Existing splits and training budgets remain.

E4.justification: v4 adds a substantial diagnostic study of how six SOP-quality configurations affect four dialogue metrics for two LLMs, examining the connection between offline and online planning. It also expands the existing cost analysis to latency and money while removing its CoT+SFT entry. Figure 4's search comparisons and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v4 introduces Spearman rank-correlation analysis between SOP F1 and dialogue accuracy, reporting 0.88 for Qwen and 0.75 for GPT. Five-fold cross-validation remains unchanged; neither version reports seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figure 4 retain their results, but v4 adds the SOP-quality findings, DPDP scores, and time/money measurements. For example, Table 6 reports GPT-4o turn accuracy of 72.29 for DPDP versus 86.37 for SGM. The CoT+SFT efficiency result disappears, and cost-analysis prose revises the stated success gain from 30% to 19%, matching the retained 22%-to-41% bars.

T1.justification: The graph and task definitions, UCT and reward formulas, human-evaluation formulas, and Algorithm 1 retain their mathematical content. The added algorithm paragraph is explanatory; no new theorem, proof, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and three main contributions retain the same dataset, SOP-guided planning framework, and effectiveness claims, including the 27.95% action-accuracy claim. The conclusion adds 'scalable' without defining a distinct extension or scaling claim.

C2.justification: v4 interprets Figure 5 as showing stronger benefits above SOP-F1 thresholds and extends the efficiency discussion to latency and money. It removes v3 Appendix A.6's interpretation that SFT offers the best performance/efficiency and excellent new-domain generalization. Hallucination and runtime limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code/data repository pointer changes from PCA-anonymous/PCA to tjunlp-lab/ChatSOP. v4 specifies a shared offline planner for cost comparisons and briefly describes the DPDP adaptation. The reported lambda value is revised; hardware, fine-tuning settings, and substantive prompt instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds an RL dialogue-policy discussion citing Du et al., Dong et al., and He et al., alongside other dialogue and reasoning references. References to Wei et al.'s CoT paper, Refiner, and ToolQA are removed. The central positioning around SOP-constrained planning remains.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites clarify offline versus online planning and expand related work. Analysis and case studies become separate subsections, the appendix cost discussion is revised into the main text, and affiliations, acknowledgments, wording, and cross-references are updated. Most technical prose and appendices remain.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 5 and Table 6, redraws the appendix cost chart as main-text Figure 6, relabels Figure 1, and expands Figures 1–3 captions. Appendix screenshots are cropped, SOP illustrations reordered, and tables and prompts rearranged. Most existing graphics and the two-column presentation remain.

improvement.justification: Section 6.5 adds useful evidence about dependence on SOP quality, comparison with an adapted dual-planner baseline, and practical runtime/monetary costs. These strengthen empirical support and clarify deployment tradeoffs beyond v3's existing evaluations. Removing the CoT+SFT efficiency comparison and providing limited adaptation details temper the gains; the core benchmark evidence is unchanged.
